solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sugar in old Greek territory reportedly less common

parts.note: a deme was a district or township of ancient Attica

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are only heard, so we want what they sound like when spoken

parts.note: rarer means less common

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where some sugar was found: in an ancient Greek district, and apparently becoming scarcer.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, DEME + RARER (a deme was an ancient Greek district) comes out as the name of the sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a light brown cane sugar, named after a region of Guyana where it was produced.

clue.text: Sign with a hand that's repulsed reviewer

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the help is read in reverse

parts.note: giving someone a hand is giving them aid
a critic reviews books, films or plays

explanation.surface: A signal with the hand that drove off a critic.
explanation.walkthrough: AID reversed gives DIA, then CRITIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A diacritic is a mark added to a letter, such as an accent, so it is a written sign.

clue.text: Hide from huge bird with two tails coming in low

indicators.note: coming in means the bird goes inside the word for low

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow
the roc is a giant mythical bird; with two tails it ends with its C doubled

explanation.surface: Escaping from a giant bird with two tails by crouching low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, but it is leather. ROC with a second tail C goes into MOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a fine goatskin leather, so it is a kind of hide.

clue.text: Landing stage needed to support artillery weapon

indicators.note: in a down answer, the support goes under what it holds up, so the landing stage comes after

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
a pier is a landing stage for boats

explanation.surface: A jetty must hold up the guns of an artillery unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery is a British Army regiment; in a down answer the supporting pier sits underneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender thrusting sword, a classic fencing weapon.

clue.text: One's relations are entertaining Eurocrat soused around noon?

indicators.note: around means the drunken bureaucrat surrounds the letter for noon
soused means drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's family are amusing a drunk EU official around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like family but means things related, stories. EUROCRAT rearranged goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled storyteller, someone whose tellings of anecdotes amuse listeners.

clue.text: One found by American poet wanting wife gone?

definitions.text: One found by American poet wanting wife gone

indicators.note: gone says the letter for wife has departed from the poet's name

parts.note: Walt Whitman, the American poet of Leaves of Grass

explanation.surface: A man who wants rid of his wife hires a killer, here oddly found through a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitman without his W is the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: someone wanting his wife dead seeks out a contract killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired assassin is exactly the person a spouse wanting a partner murdered would track down and pay.

clue.text: Leader in Rome close to Spanish Pope

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: Adrian is a papal name, as of Adrian IV

explanation.surface: A Roman leader close to a Spanish pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: H, the last letter of Spanish, then ADRIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian was a Roman emperor, ruler of the empire from AD 117 to 138.

clue.text: Gabby, endlessly demanding girl about five

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: tall as in a tall order, a demanding task

indicators.note: about means the girl's name surrounds the numeral

parts.note: Kate is a girl's name
IV is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A girl called Gabby, endlessly demanding, about five years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gabby' looks like a girl's name but is the definition; 'demanding' works through the phrase a tall order.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabby is an informal adjective for chatty, inclined to talk a lot.

clue.text: Eschewing contact with others, start to assess note spies left

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: so (soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: Unsociable people noting that spies have departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial describes someone who avoids social interaction, withdrawn from company.

clue.text: Simple tune not bad but lacking introduction

indicators.note: lacking its introduction means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: fair means passable, not bad

explanation.surface: A modest verdict on a plain melody: decent, though it lacks an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIR loses its first letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a simple melody or song, as in a folk air.

clue.text: Indiscretion where rogue hostile after short strike over

indicators.note: after places the rogue and what follows behind the shortened strike
short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: to peck is to strike with a beak
a cad is a rogue or bounder
ill as in ill will, unfriendly
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A misbehaving rogue turning nasty after a brief walkout sounds like a minor scandal at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it is the bird's strike with its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a small sin or minor fault, a trivial lapse in behaviour.

clue.text: Change mind about Sappers being disloyal

indicators.note: about means the first word is wrapped around the second

parts.note: to recant is to retract a belief, to change one's mind
RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British Army's sappers

explanation.surface: Military engineers who switch allegiance are being treacherous.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; in Britain they serve in the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreant is an archaic adjective for cowardly or unfaithful, someone who betrays a cause.

clue.text: Some script — girl mostly follows it

indicators.note: follows puts the girl's shortened name after the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A note about handwriting: part of it, then a girl's name coming after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is taken literally here, not as a pronoun pointing at the script.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic is a sloping style of typeface or handwriting, so it is a kind of script.

clue.text: Stepped in time with baton

parts.note: a baton is a short rod

explanation.surface: A marcher or drum major keeping step in rhythm while twirling a baton.
explanation.definitionFit: Trod is the past tense of tread, meaning walked or put a foot down.

clue.text: Doing as ordered one's coming to conclusion

indicators.note: ordered means put into a different order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one's is I'S, I being one, giving IS

explanation.surface: Obeying instructions is reaching a conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: DOINGAS rearranged, then IS (one is: I + 'S).
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is the conclusion a doctor reaches about an illness after examination.

clue.text: Belief shattered with ends justifying means?

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A broken faith alongside the old maxim that the ends justify the means.
explanation.walkthrough: BELIEF and ENDS together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defensible can be justified; the question mark nods at the means-and-ends maxim.

clue.text: Tackle crack soldiers sent amongst leaderless group

indicators.note: sent amongst means the joke and soldiers go inside the trimmed group
leaderless means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a set is a group
a crack is a quip, a wisecrack
men are soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers sent into a group that has lost its commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack soldiers' reads as elite troops, but the two words split: a crack is a joke, and soldiers are the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is gear or kit, as in fishing tackle, so it is equipment.

clue.text: Tons in river added to maintain pressure without planning

indicators.note: in means the tons letter goes inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

indicators.note: to maintain means to hold within, so the extra word holds the pressure letter

parts.note: more means added, extra
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Heavy weights dropped in a river, with pressure kept up, all done on the fly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means spoken or done on the spot, improvised rather than prepared.

clue.text: Gaunt old American put onto man in saloon

indicators.note: put onto means the old American goes on the end of what follows
in means the man sits inside the saloon

parts.note: a saloon is a car
Dave is a man's name

explanation.surface: A thin old American sitting with a man in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' looks like a bar, but it is a British saloon car, a sedan.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadaverous means corpse-like, extremely thin and pale, as of a haggard face.

clue.text: Answer arrived about Donne's case in scholarly life

indicators.note: about means the arrival word wraps around the poet's outside letters

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: case means the outer letters, the casing, of the name

parts.note: John Donne, the metaphysical poet; the possessive points to his name's own case

explanation.surface: A reply came concerning a poet's case within academia.
explanation.walkthrough: D and E, the outside letters of DONNE, go inside CAME, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the world of universities, the academic environment and its community.

clue.text: Muddled men, fools, not quite together

indicators.note: muddled means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged
not quite means the last letter is missing

parts.note: asses are fools

explanation.surface: Confused men and fools who are not quite united.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN rearranged to ENM, then ASSES without its last letter, ASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse means all together as a group, in a body.

clue.text: Not British, Weimar dramatist is genuine

indicators.note: not means the British letters are left out of the name

parts.note: Bertolt Brecht wrote plays in Weimar-era Germany

explanation.surface: A claim that a German playwright was authentic, not British.
explanation.walkthrough: BRECHT without BR.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loanword meaning authentic or real, the true article.

clue.text: Island century or so ago banning travel

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, so

indicators.note: banning means the travel word is shut out of the word before it

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: An island, about a hundred years ago, that forbade travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or so' reads as approximately, but OR is taken whole and SO gives SIC (Latin for thus). AGO without GO leaves A.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a French island in the Mediterranean, birthplace of Napoleon.

clue.text: Time's cut short with this, might we presume?

definitions.text: Time's cut short with this, might we presume?

parts.words: Time's cut short with this, might we presume
parts.note: Father Time carries a reaping blade, so time spans are cut short with his tool

explanation.walkthrough: Time here is Old Father Time, pictured with his blade; 'cut short' is reaping.
explanation.definitionFit: A scythe is a long curved blade for mowing, the emblem carried by Father Time.

clue.text: Switching starters, badger old woman for bottle

indicators.note: switching starters means the first letters of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: to badger is to nag
mum is an informal name for one's mother, the old woman

explanation.surface: Pester your mum for a drink, but swap things round first.
explanation.walkthrough: NAG and MUM swap initial letters to make MAG NUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a large wine bottle holding twice the standard amount.

clue.text: Range of mushrooms sent back with cap trimmed

indicators.note: sent back means the word for mushrooms is read in reverse

parts.note: ceps are a kind of edible mushroom

indicators.note: trimmed means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to cap is to outdo, to trump

explanation.surface: A selection of mushrooms returned because their caps were trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: CEPS backwards is SPEC; TRUMP trimmed is TRUM. 'Cap' looks like part of the mushroom but is the verb meaning outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range, as in the spectrum of opinion.

clue.text: Natural way to achieve financial independence

parts.note: easy means relaxed, natural
a street is a way, a road

explanation.surface: Advice on an effortless route to being rich enough to live without work.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on easy street is an idiom for living in comfort with plenty of money.

clue.text: Tribesman put sash round

indicators.note: round says the word for sash is turned the other way

parts.note: an obi is the broad sash worn with a kimono

explanation.surface: A tribesman wraps a sash around himself.
explanation.walkthrough: OBI reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ibo (Igbo) are a people of south-eastern Nigeria, so one member is a tribesman.

clue.text: Tenant not so keen to give up housing

parts.note: less means not so much, to a smaller degree

indicators.note: giving up its housing means the word sheds its outer letters, the shell around it

explanation.surface: A renter who is less enthusiastic about surrendering the home.
explanation.walkthrough: LESS, then KEEN without its outside letters K and N, giving EE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds a property under a lease, which makes them a tenant.

clue.text: See great changes in cheaper accommodation

indicators.note: changes means the letters are reordered into something new

explanation.surface: An invitation to notice major changes in budget lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE and GREAT rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger class on a ship, the low-fare quarters.
